column2: AMBIENCE VARIANTS. The merged ambience (see the 'Ambient background' entry in DESIGN.md §5) scores 7/10 against design-refs/strips/Claryo_Ambiance_and_Scroll_Functionality_3.png and the founder has rejected two earlier attempts outright. OPEN that strip and Claryo_Ambient_Hero_Page.png before writing anything. Both halves must exist: (a) the FIELD - large soft bright purple blooms on pure black, continuously moving of their own accord, unbounded with no visible edge anywhere; (b) the CUSTOM OBJECT - white technical line-work over the field, representing the venue geometry Constantine measures, that AUGMENTS as the visitor scrolls each step. tests/gimmicks.spec.ts holds you to both: 'ambient field moves on its own, with no cursor input' and 'ambient field is visible, not imperceptible'. Mount with data-testid="ambient-field". Take a genuinely different MECHANISM from the other candidates - CSS gradients, canvas 2D, WebGL shader, SVG filters, layered blend modes, particle-free flow fields are all legitimately different starting points, and the founder wants to choose between approaches rather than between tunings. Product register only, never behind technical; the hero demos stay the brightest thing (§3); static under prefers-reduced-motion.

CARD ELEVATION AND HOVER - a 10/10 reference nobody has ever attempted. OPEN design-refs/strips/Claryo_Interactive_functionality.png: on hover a card RAISES and its detail appears. Apply it to the repeated card modules - use cases, value, the how-it-works steps, the stack capability cards. Also bring the Pocket card aesthetic from design-refs/Pocket-Feature-Cards-1.png and -2.png to the FAQ, which the founder scores 2/10 for engagement and calls weak relative to the rest of the page. Take a different approach from the other candidates: what raises, how detail is revealed (in place, expanding, overlay, adjacent), and how much detail. Must work as tap-to-expand on touch, must not fight the hero demos' own hover behaviour (§3, they take priority), inert under prefers-reduced-motion.

PRIVACY FIGURES AND TEXT-WALL VISUALS. tests/reveal.spec.ts fails four sections that carry a real paragraph with nothing to look at: problem, value, privacy, use cases. That is the Slingshot 2/10 anti-reference (design-refs/strips/Slingshot_Scroll.png) - 'all thats on the screen is block text and words with no diagrams, people or ambience'. Give each section something to look at, sized so it still composes within one viewport. For PRIVACY specifically the founder asked for people: anonymised figures with blurred or unresolved faces that SHOW the no-tracking claim rather than asserting it in prose. Reuse the volumetric GhostFigure idiom already in the Outputs section rather than inventing a second one; design-refs/strips/Playvision_People_Movement.png is the 10/10 reference for figures with data bound to them. §5 is absolute: no facial detail may EVER resolve. Take a different approach from the other candidates on what the visual for each section is and how the privacy figures are composed.

SELECTOR REFINEMENTS - refine the merged entry view, do not rebuild it. Three founder notes against design-refs/strips/Clary_Selector.png (10/10): (a) the small tiles/markers beside 'Museums & Galleries' and 'Gyms' are currently identical and must visually differentiate the two verticals; (b) the reference uses a WHITE ground for the entry screen and ours is black - switch to the light ground, which also makes the fade into the dark hero a stronger transition; (c) mirror the reference more closely in general - pill geometry, the weight and position of the question, the drift path to the top right. Keep testids vertical-selector, select-museums, select-gyms, and keep hero-tab-museums / hero-tab-gyms working.
